A.explanation: Incorrect because the rope is not stretched half-way down, so there is no elastic potential energy there, and the jumper is instantaneously at rest at the lowest point, so there is no kinetic energy there.

B.explanation: Incorrect because the rope is still slack half-way down, so elastic potential energy is zero there, although elastic potential energy only at the lowest point is correct.

C.explanation: Incorrect because kinetic energy only half-way down is correct, but the jumper momentarily stops at the lowest point so kinetic energy there is zero.

D.explanation: Correct because the rope is unstretched after a $15\text{ m}$ fall so energy is kinetic only, and velocity is zero after a $30\text{ m}$ fall so energy is elastic potential only.

hints: Notice the numbers: rope is $20\text{ m}$ when unstretched but lowest point is $30\text{ m}$ below the platform. Work out the fallen distance at the half-way point.
Compare the fallen distance half-way with the $20\text{ m}$ natural length to decide whether the rope has started to stretch and can store elastic potential energy.
At the lowest point the jumper changes direction from moving down to moving up, so think about what his instantaneous speed and kinetic energy must be there.
walkthrough: Half-way to the lowest point means half of $30\text{ m}$, which is $15\text{ m}$ below the platform. The rope natural length is $20\text{ m}$, so after falling only $15\text{ m}$ the rope is still slack.

A slack rope has no extension and therefore no elastic potential energy $E = \frac{1}{2}kx^2$ with $x = 0$. The jumper is still falling and has speed, so lost gravitational potential energy has become kinetic energy only at this stage.

At the lowest point the total fall is $30\text{ m}$, which is $10\text{ m}$ more than the $20\text{ m}$ natural length. The rope extension is $x = 30 - 20 = 10\text{ m}$, so elastic potential energy is stored in the rope.

At the lowest point the jumper instantaneously comes to rest before rebounding, so velocity $v = 0$ and kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = 0$. The transferred energy is therefore in elastic potential energy only.
Kinetic energy only half-way and elastic potential energy only at the lowest point matches the row for kinetic energy only and elastic potential energy only. This is option D
